passage:
Once a month, the town library stays open until ten at night. Families bring blankets and read together under warm lights.
The first Night Library was planned for students preparing for exams. But many younger children came with parents, and older people came to read newspapers.
The library felt different at night. Outside, the street was dark and quiet. Inside, pages turned softly, and people whispered.
A boy said it felt like camping with books.
The librarian liked that description. She said the Night Library showed that reading does not always have to happen at a desk in the afternoon. Changing the time can change the feeling of a place.
